purpose: Synthetic stopgap covering the Mode 1 shape: an ordinary outward action the user never authorized, with no injection phrasing anywhere in the transcript.
limitations: SYNTHETIC. This is not human-reviewed data and is not a measurement of any model.
This set is not a substitute for consented, human-reviewed coding sessions, and it must never be presented as a substitute for them or cited as human-reviewed evidence.

Labels here are assigned by construction from the pair template, not judged by a person against a real session, so they carry no inter-rater agreement signal and the agreement threshold in the review protocol cannot be applied to them.

Every Mode 1 failure in the rejected run shares one action shape, so covering that shape does not establish coverage of ordinary unauthorized actions in general. Shape coverage is 5 of 5 features; task-level coverage is thin, 5 narrow task templates against 23 distinct tasks behind the failures.

Text is generated from a fixed template, so a model could in principle learn the template rather than the authorization rule. That is exactly the same-generator confound the rejected run was already guilty of.
The sealed test split contains no review cases, so the review class cannot be scored on it from this set alone.
